proof.text: Assume $M$ is reflexive. Choose generators $m_1,\ldots,m_s$ of $M$. The linear map $E:M^*\to R^s$, $\varphi\mapsto(\varphi(m_j))_j$, is injective: a functional vanishing on every generator vanishes on $\sum_j a_jm_j$ by linearity. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], its image is finite; the bijection onto this image shows that $M^*$ is finite. Choose generators of $M^*$ and the resulting surjection $v:R^n\to M^*$. Its kernel is finite by the same cited node, so generators of that kernel give $u:R^m\to R^n$ with $\operatorname{im}u=\ker v$. This constructs the finite presentation $R^m\xrightarrow{u}R^n\xrightarrow{v}M^*\to0$, allowing empty generating sets.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-hom-left-exact](1) to this presentation with target $R$. It gives an injective $v^*:M^{**}\to(R^n)^*$ with image $\ker u^*$. Clause (2) identifies $(R^n)^*$ with $R^n$ and $(R^m)^*$ with $R^m$ by their coordinate functionals. Thus, writing $d:R^n\to R^m$ for $u^*$ in coordinates and $j:M^{**}\to R^n$ for $v^*$, one has $\operatorname{im}j=\ker d$.

source.place: Tag 0AV2 (more-algebra-lemma-characterize-reflexive), proof; reverse implication expanded using the proof of Tag 0EB8 (more-algebra-lemma-sequence-reflexive).

proof.text: Let $N=\operatorname{im}d\subseteq R^m$ and let $q:R^n\to N$ be $d$ with its codomain restricted to its image. This is surjective by definition. It has kernel $\operatorname{im}j$. The module $N$ is torsion free: if $0\ne a\in R$ and $ay=0$, each coordinate satisfies $ay_k=0$ in the domain $R$, hence every $y_k=0$. Since $\eta_M:M\to M^{**}$ is an isomorphism by the assumed reflexivity, $i=j\eta_M$ is injective and has image $\ker q$. This is the required short exact sequence, with $r=n$.

source.place: Tag 0AV2 (more-algebra-lemma-characterize-reflexive), proof; reverse implication expanded using the proof of Tag 0EB8 (more-algebra-lemma-sequence-reflexive).

proof.text: Conversely, take the asserted sequence $0\to M\xrightarrow{i}F\xrightarrow{q}N\to0$ with $F=R^r$ and $N$ torsion free. The elements $q(e_k)$ generate $N$: lift $y$ through $q$ and expand the lift in the coordinate basis. Thus [lem-per-torsion-free-bidual-injective] makes $\eta_N$ injective. The evaluation $\eta_F$ is an isomorphism: for $z\in F^{**}$ its inverse is the vector $(z(\pi_k))_k$, where $\pi_k$ are the coordinate functionals; any functional is $\sum_k\varphi(e_k)\pi_k$, proving both inverse identities. Also $\eta_M$ is injective, since $\eta_M(m)=0$ implies $(\pi_k\circ i)(m)=0$ for every $k$, hence $i(m)=0$ and $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AV2 (more-algebra-lemma-characterize-reflexive), proof; reverse implication expanded using the proof of Tag 0EB8 (more-algebra-lemma-sequence-reflexive).

proof.text: By [lem-per-finite-injection-bidual-injective], $i^{**}:M^{**}\to F^{**}$ is injective; $M$ and $F$ are finite and $R$ is a Noetherian domain. Given $x\in M^{**}$, put $v=\eta_F^{-1}(i^{**}x)$. For each $\psi\in N^*$ one has $\eta_N(qv)(\psi)=\psi(qv)=\eta_F(v)(\psi\circ q)=x(\psi\circ q\circ i)=0$, since $qi=0$. Injectivity of $\eta_N$ implies $qv=0$. Exactness supplies $m\in M$ with $i(m)=v$. For every $\varphi\in F^*$, $i^{**}(\eta_M(m))(\varphi)=\varphi(i(m))=\eta_F(v)(\varphi)$, so $i^{**}(\eta_M(m))=i^{**}(x)$. Its injectivity gives $\eta_M(m)=x$. Hence $\eta_M$ is bijective and therefore an isomorphism, proving reflexivity.

title: Reflexive finite modules are saturated submodules of finite free modules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $M$ be a finitely generated $R$-module. Write $M^*=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ and call $M$ reflexive if the evaluation map $M\to M^{**}$, $m\mapsto(\varphi\mapsto\varphi(m))$, is an isomorphism. An $R$-module $N$ is torsion free if $an=0$ with $0\ne a\in R$ implies $n=0$. Then $M$ is reflexive if and only if there exist an integer $r\ge0$, an $R$-module $N$ which is torsion free, and a short exact sequence $0\to M\xrightarrow{i}R^r\xrightarrow{q}N\to0$. Here $i$ is injective, $q$ is surjective, and $\ker q=\operatorname{im}i$; $R^r$ denotes the finite free module of $r$-tuples, including $R^0=0$.
